author: Mark Atwood
text:
Closing as won't fix. Cost-benefit analysis:

ENGINEERING IMPACT (per the bead's own description): 'small (filter values are usually shallow)'. Filter trees in practice are 1-3 levels deep with a handful of leaf conditions; cloning that Value tree is a fixed-cost handful of allocations per /query call. Not a hotspot.

FIX-PATH COSTS:
(a) Walk JSON Value directly without going through serde — duplicates serde's untagged-enum discrimination logic for Filter::Operator vs Filter::Condition. Fragile (must track serde's algorithm) and harder to read than the typed deserialize.
(b) Use Filter::deserialize(filter_val) (borrowing form via serde::Deserialize) — requires adding serde as a direct dep of this crate. Canonical mail-server already has serde as a direct dep, so this would be a canonical-template alignment win, but the per-crate AGENTS.md explicitly restricts direct deps to {jmap-types, jmap-metadata-types, jmap-server, serde_json}. Resolving that conflict is a workspace-canonical-template-alignment concern, not a clone-elimination concern.

NET: the clone IS wasteful, but the fix paths cost more than the savings warrant. Per workspace AGENTS.md 'Do not manufacture problems to fill space. Bikeshedding is a failure mode, not thoroughness' — this falls on the bikeshedding side of the line.

If/when the workspace direct-dep audit happens (a workspace-canonical-template-alignment sweep that aligns metadata-server's and other extension-server siblings' Cargo.toml direct deps with mail-server's canonical), the borrowing-Deserialize form can be applied trivially as part of that pass. Until then, the clone stays.
